title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page belongs to a short sequence (EZ1, EZ2) on the Eilenberg–Zilber–Cartier theorem and its use to build products and Steenrod operations at the level of simplicial abelian groups. This is presumably background for the divided-power de Rham complex talk. The previous page sets up Dold–Kan normalization N, the diagonal versus total complex of a bisimplicial abelian group, the shuffle (Eilenberg–Zilber) and Alexander–Whitney maps, and the cup product.

On this page Grothendieck builds a simplicial model of the cup-product pairing of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces, K(Z,i) × K(Z,j) → K(Z,i+j).
- Take K(Z,n) to be the simplicial abelian group Γ(Z[n]) obtained by Dold–Kan.
- The product map factors through the degreewise tensor product: the bilinear map K(Z,i) × K(Z,j) → K(Z,i) ⊗ K(Z,j), followed by a homomorphism f of simplicial abelian groups K(Z,i) ⊗ K(Z,j) → K(Z,i+j).
- By Dold–Kan, N is an equivalence of categories, so 'il suffit de construire Nf'. That is, one only needs a chain map N(K(Z,i) ⊗ K(Z,j)) → N K(Z,i+j) = Z[i+j].
- This is obtained as a composite. First the Eilenberg–Zilber map from the normalized complex of the diagonal tensor product to the tensor product of normalized complexes, N(A ⊗ B) → NA ⊗ NB; in this direction it is concretely the Alexander–Whitney map. Then the identification Z[i] ⊗ Z[j] = Z[i+j].
- Applying Dold–Kan's inverse gives f, hence the pairing. Through representability H^n(X,Z) = [X, K(Z,n)], this recovers the cup product, as at the end of the previous page.

A crossed-out block at the bottom records an unrelated aside. It reads: (Inv^G(S g*), H*(G, L Sym g*)) ⇒ H*(BG). This says that the cohomology of a classifying space is computed from invariant polynomials on the Lie algebra (Chern–Weil), or more precisely from group cohomology of G with coefficients in the derived symmetric powers of g*, presumably via a spectral sequence.

The next page goes on to E∞-type structure via W_n = Z EΣ_n and to Steenrod operations.
errors: The map labelled 'E.Z.' goes N(A⊗B) → NA⊗NB. In standard terminology that direction is the Alexander–Whitney map; the shuffle (Eilenberg–Zilber) map goes the other way. Either map works here up to homotopy, so this is only a labelling point.
No gap otherwise: Dold–Kan does reduce the construction of f to constructing Nf.

ideas.what: Construct the cup-product pairing K(Z,i)×K(Z,j)→K(Z,i+j) simplicially, via Dold–Kan plus Eilenberg–Zilber/Alexander–Whitney.
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial model of the cup product on Eilenberg–MacLane spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg–MacLane, Dold–Kan, May (Simplicial Objects in Algebraic Topology)

ideas.what: Crossed-out: H*(BG) computed from invariant polynomials Inv^G(Sym g*), or from H*(G, L Sym g*).
ideas.modern_name: Chern–Weil / Bott–Totaro computation of Hodge (de Rham) cohomology of BG: H^i(BG, Ω^j) = H^{i-j}(G, S^j g*)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Chern–Weil; Bott (1973); Totaro (Hodge theory of classifying stacks, 2018)

missed.claim: In a mid-1970s note on divided-power de Rham theory, Grothendieck jots down that H*(BG) should be computed from group cohomology of G with coefficients in derived symmetric powers of g* (generalizing invariant polynomials). This anticipates the algebraic, characteristic-p-sensitive form of the Bott/Totaro theorem on Hodge cohomology of classifying stacks. The use of 'L Sym' suggests he saw that derived symmetric powers are the correct coefficients outside characteristic 0.
missed.quote: Inv^G(Sg*) / H*(G, L Sym g*) ⇒ H*(BG)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modestly: this is an early record of the idea behind Totaro's 2018 work and the derived-Sym or crystalline viewpoint on BG. But it is crossed out, a single line with no development, and Bott had the smooth version by 1973.

deep.surprise_reason: The main content is the textbook construction of cup products via Dold–Kan and Eilenberg–Zilber. Only the crossed-out aside with L Sym g* hints at something beyond routine, and it is too fragmentary to count for much.
transcription_corrections: The first line should end 'K(Z, i+j)' with a closing parenthesis.
The arrow from K(Z,i)×K(Z,j) points down to K(Z,i)⊗K(Z,j); the map f goes from that tensor product up to K(Z,i+j), completing a triangle.
The bottom block (Inv^G(S g*), H*(G, L Sym g*) ⇒ H*(BG)) is enclosed in parentheses and struck through with a large X.
